div.div: Information Nexus for investigating telemetry delivery characteristics, timestamp integrity and event ingestion timeliness evidence.

div.p: What this shows: Summary delivery delay statistics for the selected telemetry sample.
How it is calculated: Delay is calculated as _indextime - _time. Median and percentile values are less sensitive to outliers than a simple average.

Read it as: High delay can indicate delivery backlog, batch collection, API polling delay, or incorrect timestamp extraction. Use the timestamp panels to separate expected delay from timestamp quality issues.

search.query: | stats count as events_sampled median(ingest_delay_seconds) as median_delay_seconds perc95(ingest_delay_seconds) as p95_delay_seconds max(ingest_delay_seconds) as max_delay_seconds count(eval(delay_category="Healthy")) as healthy_delay_events count(eval(delay_category="Warning")) as warning_delay_events count(eval(delay_category="Poor")) as poor_delay_events count(eval(delay_category="Critical")) as critical_delay_events count(eval(timestamp_indicator="Future timestamp")) as future_timestamp_events count(eval(timestamp_indicator="Old event at index time")) as old_event_at_index_events | eval median_delay=case(abs(median_delay_seconds)<60,tostring(round(median_delay_seconds,0))."s",abs(median_delay_seconds)<3600,tostring(round(median_delay_seconds/60,1))."m",abs(median_delay_seconds)<86400,tostring(round(median_delay_seconds/3600,1))."h",true(),tostring(round(median_delay_seconds/86400,1))."d") | eval p95_delay=case(abs(p95_delay_seconds)<60,tostring(round(p95_delay_seconds,0))."s",abs(p95_delay_seconds)<3600,tostring(round(p95_delay_seconds/60,1))."m",abs(p95_delay_seconds)<86400,tostring(round(p95_delay_seconds/3600,1))."h",true(),tostring(round(p95_delay_seconds/86400,1))."d") | eval max_delay=case(abs(max_delay_seconds)<60,tostring(round(max_delay_seconds,0))."s",abs(max_delay_seconds)<3600,tostring(round(max_delay_seconds/60,1))."m",abs(max_delay_seconds)<86400,tostring(round(max_delay_seconds/3600,1))."h",true(),tostring(round(max_delay_seconds/86400,1))."d") | eval worst_observed_status=case(future_timestamp_events>0,"Future timestamp",critical_delay_events>0,"Critical",poor_delay_events>0,"Poor",warning_delay_events>0,"Warning",true(),"Healthy") | rename events_sampled as "Events Sampled" | rename median_delay as "Median Delay" | rename p95_delay as "P95 Delay" | rename max_delay as "Max Delay" | rename healthy_delay_events as "Healthy" | rename warning_delay_events as "Warning" | rename poor_delay_events as "Poor" | rename critical_delay_events as "Critical" | rename future_timestamp_events as "Future Timestamps" | rename old_event_at_index_events as "Over 30 Days Old" | rename worst_observed_status as "Worst Status" | table "Events Sampled" "Median Delay" "P95 Delay" "Max Delay" Healthy Warning Poor Critical "Future Timestamps" "Over 30 Days Old" "Worst Status"

div.p: What this shows: The active and excluded rules from the telemetry_timeliness_rules lookup.
How to use it: Confirm that the selected source or sourcetype has the expected thresholds. poor_seconds is the upper boundary for Poor; anything above it is Critical.
Rule matching: The evidence search checks the selected grouping rule first, then source, then sourcetype, then an optional default,* row, then dashboard fallback thresholds.

search.query: | inputlookup telemetry_timeliness_rules | eval status=if(enabled=0,"Excluded","Active") | eval healthy_range="<= " . healthy_seconds . "s" | eval warning_range="> " . healthy_seconds . "s and <= " . warning_seconds . "s" | eval poor_range="> " . warning_seconds . "s and <= " . poor_seconds . "s" | eval critical_range="> " . poor_seconds . "s" | rename object_type as "Object Type" | rename object_name as "Object Name" | rename status as "Status" | rename healthy_range as "Healthy" | rename warning_range as "Warning" | rename poor_range as "Poor" | rename critical_range as "Critical" | rename notes as "Notes" | table "Object Type" "Object Name" Status Healthy Warning Poor Critical Notes | sort "Object Type" "Object Name"

div.p: What this shows: Events grouped into configurable delivery-delay buckets.
How to use it: A small number of delayed events may be normal for batch or cloud sources. A broad shift into Warning, Poor, or Critical usually deserves investigation.
Configuration: Thresholds and exclusions are controlled by the telemetry_timeliness_rules lookup, not by dashboard inputs. Use enabled=0 to exclude a source or sourcetype from this view.

search.query: | stats count by delay_category | appendpipe [ stats count as _seed | eval delay_category=split("Healthy,Warning,Poor,Critical,Future timestamp",",") | mvexpand delay_category | eval count=0 | fields delay_category count ] | stats sum(count) as count by delay_category | eval sort_order=case(delay_category="Healthy",1,delay_category="Warning",2,delay_category="Poor",3,delay_category="Critical",4,delay_category="Future timestamp",5,true(),99) | sort sort_order | rename delay_category as "Delay Category" | rename count as "Events" | fields "Delay Category" Events

div.p: What this shows: Median delivery delay over time for the selected telemetry.
How to use it: Look for step changes or rising trends that indicate collection, queueing, or platform delivery changes during the selected period.

search.query: | timechart median(ingest_delay_seconds) as "Median Delay" perc95(ingest_delay_seconds) as "P95 Delay"

div.p: What this shows: Delivery delay metrics grouped by the selected grouping field.
How to use it: Sort by p95 or max delay to find sources with intermittent delivery problems. Sort by future or old timestamp counts to identify timestamp extraction problems.

div.p: What this shows: Events whose event time is ahead of index time, or already more than 30 days old when indexed.

How to use it: Future timestamps usually indicate source clock skew, timezone handling, or timestamp parsing issues. They are important to surface because future-dated events can be missed by time-bounded searches and detections until the event time becomes current. Events over 30 days old at index time may be normal for intentional backfill, but can also indicate parser issues or unexpected historical replay.

search.query: | stats count by timestamp_indicator | appendpipe [ stats count as _seed | eval timestamp_indicator=split("Within configured bounds,Future timestamp,Old event at index time",",") | mvexpand timestamp_indicator | eval count=0 | fields timestamp_indicator count ] | stats sum(count) as count by timestamp_indicator | eval sort_order=case(timestamp_indicator="Within configured bounds",1,timestamp_indicator="Future timestamp",2,timestamp_indicator="Old event at index time",3,true(),99) | sort sort_order | eval timestamp_indicator=case(timestamp_indicator="Old event at index time","Over 30 days old at index",true(),timestamp_indicator) | rename timestamp_indicator as "Timestamp Integrity" | rename count as "Events" | fields "Timestamp Integrity" Events

div.p: What this shows: Median, p90, p95 and maximum delivery delay by Data Source, evaluated against the rule applied to that source or sourcetype.
How to use it: Compare the percentile statuses and critical boundary to confirm whether the observed delay actually crosses the configured lookup thresholds.

search.query: | stats median(ingest_delay_seconds) as median_seconds p90(ingest_delay_seconds) as p90_seconds p95(ingest_delay_seconds) as p95_seconds max(ingest_delay_seconds) as max_seconds values(timeliness_rule_source) as rule_source max(healthy_seconds) as healthy_seconds max(warning_seconds) as warning_seconds max(poor_seconds) as poor_seconds values(poor_display) as poor_display by group_value | eval median_status=case(median_seconds<0,"Future timestamp",median_seconds<=healthy_seconds,"Healthy",median_seconds<=warning_seconds,"Warning",median_seconds<=poor_seconds,"Poor",true(),"Critical") | eval p90_status=case(p90_seconds<0,"Future timestamp",p90_seconds<=healthy_seconds,"Healthy",p90_seconds<=warning_seconds,"Warning",p90_seconds<=poor_seconds,"Poor",true(),"Critical") | eval p95_status=case(p95_seconds<0,"Future timestamp",p95_seconds<=healthy_seconds,"Healthy",p95_seconds<=warning_seconds,"Warning",p95_seconds<=poor_seconds,"Poor",true(),"Critical") | eval max_status=case(max_seconds<0,"Future timestamp",max_seconds<=healthy_seconds,"Healthy",max_seconds<=warning_seconds,"Warning",max_seconds<=poor_seconds,"Poor",true(),"Critical") | eval critical_boundary=">" . tostring(poor_seconds) . "s (" . mvindex(poor_display,0) . ")" | rename median_seconds as median p90_seconds as p90 p95_seconds as p95 max_seconds as max | foreach median p90 p95 max [ eval <<FIELD>>=case(abs(<<FIELD>>)<60,tostring(round(<<FIELD>>,0))."s",abs(<<FIELD>>)<3600,tostring(round(<<FIELD>>/60,1))."m",abs(<<FIELD>>)<86400,tostring(round(<<FIELD>>/3600,1))."h",true(),tostring(round(<<FIELD>>/86400,1))."d") ] | rename group_value as "Data Source" | rename rule_source as "Rule Source" | rename median as "Median" | rename median_status as "Median Status" | rename p90 as "P90" | rename p90_status as "P90 Status" | rename p95 as "P95" | rename p95_status as "P95 Status" | rename max as "Max" | rename max_status as "Max Status" | rename critical_boundary as "Critical Boundary" | table "Data Source" "Rule Source" Median "Median Status" P90 "P90 Status" P95 "P95 Status" Max "Max Status" "Critical Boundary" | sort "Data Source"

div.p: What this shows: Example events with the highest measured delivery delay in the selected sample.
How to use it: Use these examples to determine whether delay is caused by real collection backlog, source replay, batch collection, or timestamp extraction problems.
Evidence: Raw events are intentionally shown as representative evidence and truncated only for display safety.
